gaps.category: Stray and gap sectors under state/municipal licensing: restaurants and fondas (licencia de funcionamiento, Protección Civil programa interno, Aviso COFEPRIS), cantinas, and Protección Civil annual programme for all small premises

gaps.why: Every small premises in Mexico needs a state/municipal Protección Civil programa interno or dictamen with annual renewal, plus licencia de funcionamiento refrendo and uso de suelo. Table only touched Protección Civil within nurseries and alcohol; the horizontal duty across millions of premises is not tested, and fragmentation by state is itself the opportunity.

coverage.category: 1. Household employers: domestic workers, live-in carers, nannies
coverage.found: Nothing new beyond K27/K30 (IMSS domestic-worker registration). No search spent, as the idea is already known and rechecked.

coverage.category: 2. Scrap-metal dealers
coverage.found: No federal register or reporting duty found. Only municipal rules exist, for example a Tizimín, Yucatán reglamento on copper and aluminium buyers and a 2013 Nuevo León bill proposing municipal registers. A patchwork of local rules makes a national product hard. Listed as a weak candidate.

coverage.category: 3. Second-hand dealers and pawnbrokers
coverage.found: Pawnbrokers are known (K28): PROFECO registry, 4,042 shops, annual renewal. 'Autos chocolate' regularisation decree was abrogated at end-2025, so no recurring duty (rejected). Used-goods dealers outside pawn: no register found.

coverage.category: 4. Gold and jewellery buyers
coverage.found: Jewellers and precious-metal traders are an LFPIORPI vulnerable activity (art. 17 fr. VI), reformed Jul 2025, with a regulation reform on 27 Mar 2026. KYC Systems already sells a dedicated precious-metals product. It is a different buyer group from K07/K08 but is crowded. Weak candidate.

coverage.category: 5. Used car parts and vehicle dismantlers
coverage.found: Both searches returned only Argentine material. No Mexican dismantler register or reporting duty confirmed (NOM-161 and REPUVE are unverified for this trade). Unverified.

coverage.category: 6. Livestock traders, markets and animal transport
coverage.found: Nothing new beyond K05 (cattle movements, REEMO guías). Guía issue is state-run; Coahuila guía valid 5 days, fee about MXN 145 [state RETYS page]. SINIIGA v6 started 20 Apr 2026 (headline only, unverified).

coverage.category: 7. Small abattoirs and butchers
coverage.found: Municipal rastros (TSS) and TIF plants are run or reviewed by municipalities, Salud or SENASICA. The buyer is often a municipality, not a small business. Carnicería duties are municipal. Nothing new.

coverage.category: 8. Beekeepers
coverage.found: SENASICA honey-traceability scheme: beekeepers, collectors and packers get a clave ID, updated yearly, and a UPP key via SINIIGA windows. Tiny annual duty, low willingness to pay. Weak.

coverage.category: 9. Veterinary practices and veterinary medicine sellers
coverage.found: Group I drugs need a recetas cuantificadas with SENASICA-authorised folios (50 folios first time). A copy must be kept 1 year by the seller and the applicator. A SENASICA/WOAH presentation describes monthly Excel reports emailed to the Secretaría and delays in obtaining folios. SENASICA planned an electronic traceability system; whether it is live is unverified. New candidate.

coverage.category: 10. Well drillers and water abstraction
coverage.found: New Ley General de Aguas (DOF 11 Dec 2025) plus a CONAGUA first-phase regularisation accord (DOF 15 Jul 2026), with a one-year window to 15 Jul 2027. Eligible holders need a meter, 2 years of volume records and 5 years of fee payments. Fetched the Garrigues summary. A strong deadline-driven candidate. No driller-specific register found.

coverage.category: 11. Septic, sanitation and waste haulers
coverage.found: Special-waste (RME) transport needs state authorisation, with state-specific papers such as land-use, impact-authorisation and accident-prevention programme in Coahuila, and a disposal receipt and inspection in Zacatecas. Hazardous waste needs federal SEMARNAT authorisation and a manifest. The septic-sludge rules are unclear. Related to K01 (RPBI/used oil).

coverage.category: 12. Lift, boiler and pressure-equipment owners and inspectors
coverage.found: NOM-020-STPS: STPS accord of 31 Aug 2026 merged the two NOM-020 avisos into one 'solicitud de número de control' (STPS-08-003) for category III equipment. A third-party dictamen is still needed. No lift register found; NOM-053/NOM-207 are product and maintenance standards. Weak.

coverage.category: 13. Small water systems
coverage.found: Ley General de Aguas recognises and provides for inscribing community water systems. The exact duties and deadlines are not confirmed, and the buyers are village committees with little money. Unverified.

coverage.category: 14. Pesticide and fertiliser dealers and applicators
coverage.found: NOM-033-FITO-1995 requires dealers to file an aviso de inicio de funcionamiento, be certified by a Tercero Especialista Autorizado, and keep a log of written recommendations, buyers and quantities. They also keep control of product registration numbers and send a supplier list to SENASICA every 2 years. NOM-052-FITO covers aerial applicators (aviso and bitácora). No dealer software found. No fertiliser rules found.

coverage.category: 15. Labour contractors and recruitment agencies
coverage.found: Agencias de colocación need STPS authorisation and file a quarterly participation report. A STPS simplification accord of 9 Jun 2026 merged procedures. REPSE has a single homoclave from 2026. Covered by payroll-bridge idea K03 and security/cleaning idea K02. Weak.

coverage.category: 16. Cemeteries, burial societies and funeral services
coverage.found: Funeral firms hold a licencia sanitaria or aviso at state COFEPRIS-equivalent bodies, and transfers need notice to the health authority (LGS 350 Bis 1). Rules differ by state, with a Dec 2025 federal proposal to treat funeral services as a public service. No recurring report found. Weak.

coverage.category: 17. Community and religious bodies: associations, charities, halal and kosher supervision
coverage.found: Donatarias autorizadas: annual transparency declaration (31 May), donativos CFDI with donataria complement, electronic accounting. SAT revoked 270 authorisations in 2025. No donataria-specific software surfaced. Religious associations and halal/kosher bodies: not searched.

coverage.category: 18. Transport operators: minibus, taxi, moto-taxi, small trucking and bus fleets
coverage.found: Taxis: CDMX padrón (23k drivers), SLP revista 2026 and the Mi Taxi app. These are state-run and varied. Federal trucking: 25+ SICT procedures cut to 9, licence digitalisation, SIRSE for auxiliary services. Carta Porte is known and rejected (K25). Nothing new that is promising.

coverage.category: 19. Market traders, street vendors, money changers
coverage.found: Currency exchange needs CNBV registration (RECC-TD, over 2,000 centros, 259 sanctions Jan 2024 to Jul 2025). The AML side is crowded (K23). No federal duty for street vendors, only municipal permits.

coverage.category: 20. Small licensed premises with inspections: tattoo studios, driving schools, childminders and nurseries, small food producers, hunting outfitters
coverage.found: Hunting outfitters and UMAs: annual report in Apr-Jun (RLGVS art. 50), cintillo tags, and a report within 30 days of each hunting service on public land. New candidate. Tattoo studios: aviso, tarjeta de control sanitario and a bound logbook kept 2 years (weak, small niche). Driving schools: CDMX guidelines of 27 Mar 2024 and a Morelos draft in 2026 (state-specific). Nurseries (CAI): local registries refreshed every 6 months and Protección Civil programmes by state. Small food producers: not searched.

coverage.category: 21. Fuel stations and fuel or LPG distributors
coverage.found: Federal. SAT volumetric controls (monthly report, daily report, lab dictamen) already known as K26. New 2026 angle: CNE (successor to CRE) DOF 21-Jan-2026 acuerdo setting the maximum-price methodology for LP gas sold to end users, binding on holders of commercialisation/distribution/retail permits (via Cuatrecasas note, not the DOF text). No small-operator regime found. No new 2026 cylinder-verification rule found.

coverage.category: 22. Grain, coffee, cocoa and other commodity traders, millers and warehouses
coverage.found: Thin. Only an undated ASERCA procedure for registering/updating centros de acopio and tracking incentive-linked inventories, and a 2026 Sinaloa white-maize marketing support (window to 1-Aug-2026) aimed at producers. Nothing found on coffee or cocoa trader duties, nor a SENASICA traceability duty for warehouses. Almacenes generales de depósito are CNBV-regulated and not small.

coverage.category: 23. Co-operatives, credit unions and savings groups
coverage.found: Federal. SOCAPs report monthly to CNBV through SITI (Circular Única arts. 307-310; series R08, R17, R21, R24-B). Instructivos date 2015-2023, nothing new for 2026. A 'nivel básico' tier exists, with no lighter reporting confirmed. Vendors and competition not checked.

coverage.category: 24. Private clinics, labs and other health providers that bill insurers or state schemes
coverage.found: Federal. COFEPRIS aviso de funcionamiento y responsable sanitario (form COFEPRIS-05-036 for consultorios, dental clinics and labs without X-ray) is a one-time notice plus change/baja notices, with no periodic renewal found. Ley General de Salud reform published 15-Jan-2026: telemedicine has the same legal validity as in-person care, and COFEPRIS gained electronic verification visits. No insurer-billing duty was screened. No recurring filing found.

coverage.category: 25. Pharmacies, medicine importers, and users of controlled chemicals or precursors
coverage.found: Federal, with state health services receiving filings. Pharmacies with a sanitary licence for controlled drugs need authorised physical control books (one per group) and file purchase/sale 'previsiones' notices (COFEPRIS-03-014 semiannual, 03-004 annual; the sources contradict each other and are aggregator pages). No official e-book rule found. LFCPQ art. 7 requires an annual report on precursor chemicals through COFEPRIS; PISE Anexo 10 sector 3 covers precursors. A 2026 article claims tramadol became a controlled drug on 14-Jul-2026 (unverified, secondary source).

coverage.category: 26. Security, cleaning and manpower agencies, and the firms that hire their workers
coverage.found: Federal and state. REPSE registrants must file ICSOE (IMSS, LSS art. 15-A) and SISUB (INFONAVIT, art. 29 Bis) every four months, due 17 Jan, 17 May and 17 Sep, with joint liability for the client. Private security: Ley Federal de Seguridad Privada requires companies to keep the Registro Nacional de Empresas, Personal y Equipo current (Reglamento arts. 32-34: alta/baja with reasons, uniform models, vehicles, arms, radios, training, evaluations). DGSP sanctions published in 2026 for omitted baja of 112 uniforms and branches. The Ley General de Seguridad Privada required by the 2021 constitutional reform was still unpublished when last found. K02 (hours registry) is a different duty.

coverage.category: 27. Construction, mining and quarry contractors and suppliers: site registers, accreditation, local-content reports
coverage.found: Construction is covered by REPSE/ICSOE/SISUB (see 26). The quarry and small-mining search returned only Ecuador, Peru, Chile and Argentina, with nothing for Mexico, so Mexican quarry, bancos de materiales and explosives-use duties were not reached. Local-content reports do not appear to apply.

coverage.category: 28. Notaries, land agents, real estate brokers and other professionals with periodic or anti-money-laundering reports
coverage.found: Federal. LFPIORPI reform (16-Jul-2025) took art. 18 duties from 7 to 13: risk-based approach, manual, annual training, automated transactional profile, annual audit, 10-year file retention. Reglamento reform DOF 27-Mar-2026 adds PEP checks, a 24-hour attempted-operation aviso and 6-month accumulation. Acuerdo 115/2026 (DOF 7-Aug-2026) has an obligations calendar starting Nov 2026. Estate agents fall under fracc. V, and developers under V Bis (aviso from 8,025 UMA). All of this matches known K07-K23, so nothing new.

coverage.category: 29. Hotels, guest houses and short-term rentals: guest registers, tourism levies
coverage.found: Federal and state. The Registro Nacional de Turismo is mandatory under Ley General de Turismo art. 48 (30 days from start of operations), with one paragraph reportedly struck down by the SCJN. A national guest-register duty exists only as a bill (art. 59 Bis LGT, aimed at registering minors). SAT online access to platform data from 1-Apr-2026 (CFF 30-B), with platforms withholding ISR/IVA. The state lodging tax (ISH) varies by state. No federal guest-register law in force found.

coverage.category: 30. Small exporters and importers facing traceability or certification rules: food, fish, timber, forest-risk commodities
coverage.found: Federal. Padrón de Importadores and Padrón de Sectores Específicos (Ley Aduanera art. 59-IV, RGCE 2026 Anexo 10 published DOF 14-Jan-2026, sectors include chemicals, precursors, firearms, explosives and others). 2026 changes: letter of credit allowed as guarantee, new suspension causes, random SAT address checks on registration. Customs brokers handle this, so little direct need for software. IMMEX annual report claims came only from blogs. Timber is K04 and fishing is K06. No new food or fish traceability duty found.

coverage.category: 31. Pyrotechnics, explosives and arms retailers (SEDENA permits)
coverage.found: Federal (SEDENA), with state/municipal layers. Pyrotechnics sellers need a permiso general under the Ley Federal de Armas de Fuego y Explosivos. Reglamento art. 83 requires a monthly operations report (purchases and sales with counterparties), within 10 days per the Reglamento, and 5 days per another source. Art. 60 allows up to 10 kg of sales to individuals without a permit. A Protección Civil dictamen and a municipal sales permit are also required. Seasonal and highly local. The sources are news and an old regulation text.

coverage.category: 32. Water concession holders and users (CONAGUA / Ley General de Aguas 2025)
coverage.found: Federal, with state harmonisation within 180 days. The Ley General de Aguas plus Ley de Aguas Nacionales reforms were published in the DOF on 11-Dec-2025 and took effect the next day. Concessions can no longer be transferred between private parties; CONAGUA reassigns them; use change is barred; unused concessions revert; REPDA is replaced by a Registro Nacional del Agua; fines are reportedly up to 50,000 UMA. The meter duty stays from the Ley de Aguas Nacionales. The transitory articles on existing wells and small users were not found.

coverage.category: 33. Alcohol sellers and artisanal spirits producers (licences, IEPS marbetes, mezcal)
coverage.found: State and municipal licences (alcohol licence from the Tesorería or state alcohol law, with Protección Civil dictamen and uso de suelo). Federal: IEPS marbetes; IEPS on high-ABV spirits reportedly 53% in 2026; several reform proposals for artisanal-producer relief in 2025-26 that were unconfirmed as enacted. Duties are fragmented across 32 states and municipalities.

coverage.category: 34. Mobile-line registration (CRT, Dec 2025)
coverage.found: Federal. CRT Lineamientos published in the DOF on 9-Dec-2025 oblige carriers and comercializadoras to link lines to CURP/RFC. The Jun-2026 deadline was reportedly extended 184 days, with carrier SMS campaigns (one outlet, unconfirmed). No duty found for small retailers or distributors. This is mostly a consumer-side duty.

coverage.category: 35. Gaming and sweepstakes permit holders (SEGOB)
coverage.found: Federal. The Ley Federal de Juegos y Sorteos (1947) reform is in SEGOB review and had not been confirmed as sent to Congress. The IEPS on bets and sweepstakes rose from 30% to 50% from 1-Jan-2026. Permit holders report income monthly to the Dirección General de Juegos y Sorteos (2019 ASF audit). Segob dismissed its Director General in 2026. AML (LFPIORPI) also applies. The buyer group is mostly large operators, so little to build.

coverage.category: 36. Hazardous-waste microgenerators (consultorios, dental clinics, vets, workshops)
coverage.found: Federal and local. LGPGIR art. 48 requires microgenerators to register and hand waste to authorised collectors. SEMARNAT-07-017 covers registration and 07-031 covers updates. The annual COA (1 Mar-30 Jun) falls on large generators and service providers, not microgenerators. Closure notice exists. K01 covers the collectors' side, this one the generators' side.
